name: Wind changes no number the fit writes
non_visual_rationale: Byte-identity of a stored prefix, established by diffing JSON text between two runs; no rendered surface is involved at any point in the comparison. U1-U8 and a Vera walk are therefore N/A, and inventing pixel checks for a byte comparison would be evidence of nothing.
criteria: Rotating the wind word on every morning leaves everything stored under the corrections prefix byte-identical.
No wind residual, no wind bias and no wind standard error exists anywhere in the fit.
Stored timestamps come from the injected clock, so re-running the same inputs writes the same bytes.
scope_note: The acceptance oracle snapshots the corrections prefix as the fit actually writes it today: one current/<spot_id>.json key. 06 section 7's aggregate contract also declares a history/dt= copy per run, which src/learning/fit.ts does not yet write. That gap is flagged, not built here: writing it would be production behaviour no scenario in this step demands.
acceptance: Twenty generated cases run the nightly fit three times over 10-30 paired mornings whose wind words are rotated by 1-2 positions, then a fourth time on a later injected clock. The oracle asserts the whole corrections prefix is byte-identical across the rotation and across a re-run, that no stored body matches /wind/i, and that computed_at equals the injected clock in both runs. It rejects a controlled single-byte computed_at mutation and a controlled wind_bias field.
falsifiability_proof: Two separate mutations of src/learning/correction-file.ts. (1) Emitting a wind_bias derived from the reported wind word failed both the acceptance byte-identity oracle and the unit emitter law ('rotating the wind word must leave every emitted byte identical'). (2) Replacing clock.now().toISOString() with a hardcoded literal failed the clock-provenance oracle ('must stamp the injected clock, never the ambient one'). Both were reverted and `git diff --stat src/` confirmed empty before the gate was re-run.
